home.title: Piggybow: a friendly money journal
home.description: A friendly money journal with a pig who never judges.
home.headline: Piggybow
home.tagline: A friendly money journal with a pig who never judges.
home.body: Note what you spend and save, watch a rainbow fill in as you reach your goals, and get small, kind ideas for saving. No bank login, no account: your entries stay with you.
home.comingSoon: Coming soon to Android and iPhone.

support.title: Help & contact · Piggybow
support.description: Write to us at {supportEmail}. We read every message.
support.headline: Help & contact
support.write: Write to us at {supportEmail}. We read every message. If you email us, we get your email address and your message and use them only to reply. Emails to {supportEmail} are passed on to our mailbox by Forward Email, an email-forwarding service.

stored.a: On your phone, and in your phone's own backup (Google) if you've turned it on; on Android, only when that backup is end-to-end encrypted. On iPhone, your journal isn't in your iCloud backup. Piggybow has no account and no server for your money notes.

newPhone.q: Can I move to a new phone?
newPhone.a: On Android, yes: to a new Android phone, if your phone backs up your apps, restore that backup on the new phone. Piggybow is only in a cloud backup when your phone has a screen lock, so the backup is encrypted. Android 8 and older don't back it up at all. App lock turns off after a restore, so turn it on again in Me. On iPhone, your journal isn't in your iCloud backup, so restoring one won't bring it back. Moving between Android and iPhone isn't possible yet. You can always keep a copy: Me → Export my data gives you a spreadsheet file (CSV) to save or send.

delete.q: How do I delete my data?
delete.a: In the app, go to Me → Delete all my data. That erases everything Piggybow stored on your phone. Your journal is never stored with us. If you turned on pig tips, it also deletes the random ID, its IP address and the daily count our server keeps for them. On Android, copies in your phone's own backup are managed in your Google account settings.

advice.a: No. The pig's ideas are everyday saving habits, not financial, tax or investment advice.

tips.q: What are pig tips, and what do they send?
tips.a: If you turn them on, your pig uses AI to suggest one idea a day that fits your week. Piggybow sends a short summary in numbers, like what share of your spending went to food. Never your notes, amounts or anything you typed. Turn them off anytime in Me → Pig tips. The privacy policy has the details.

pin.a: Tap "Forgot PIN?" and use your phone's own screen lock (fingerprint, face, PIN or pattern) to get in, then choose a new PIN. If your phone has no screen lock, the only way back in is to erase Piggybow's data on your phone and start over.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: How Piggybow handles your money notes: they stay on your phone.

who.body: Piggybow is made by BurrowSoft, Thailand. You can reach us at {supportEmail}. If you email us, we get your email address and your message and use them only to reply. Emails to {supportEmail} are passed on to our mailbox by Forward Email, an email-forwarding service.

stores.intro: Piggybow keeps what you type in it:
stores.entries: your spends and saves: amounts, categories, notes, and how a spend felt;
stores.settings: your settings: currency, what makes your pig happy, your weekly plan, reminder time, app lock and appearance.
stores.onPhone: All of it is stored on your phone. If you turn on the app lock, your PIN is kept in your phone's secure storage.
stores.backup: On Android, if your phone backs up its apps to your Google account, that backup can include Piggybow's entries and settings, but only when the backup is end-to-end encrypted, which needs a screen lock on your phone. Android 8 and older don't back it up at all. The backup belongs to your Google account, and we can't see it. On iPhone, Piggybow keeps your journal out of iCloud Backup; a few app settings, like language and appearance, can be in it. Your app-lock PIN never moves to another phone.

leaves.body: Your journal doesn't. Piggybow has no account and no server for your money notes.
leaves.tipsLabel: Pig tips, only if you turn them on.
leaves.tips: Piggybow can ask an AI to write your pig's tip of the day. To do that, it sends our server a short summary in numbers: what share of your spending went to each built-in category, how many spends felt worth it, how far along your plan and goal are (in %), what you said makes your pig happy, your language and the day of the week. It never sends your notes, amounts, dates, goal names or anything you typed.
leaves.tipsWho: Our server runs on Supabase in the USA, and the summary is passed to Anthropic (USA), whose AI writes the tip. Anthropic doesn't use it to train AI models and deletes it within 30 days, unless it's flagged for a safety review or the law requires longer. Our server keeps a random app ID, the IP address it last connected from, and a count of tips per day, to keep the service fair. The counts are deleted after 30 days, and the ID with its IP address after 30 days without tips. Supabase's logs also keep the IP address for up to 7 days, to protect the service from abuse. If you report a tip, we keep that tip's text and the reason you chose, without your ID, for 90 days to improve our filter. Turn tips off in Me → Pig tips, or use Delete all my data, and we delete that ID, its IP address and its count as soon as your phone is online.
leaves.transfer: Supabase and Anthropic are in the USA, so pig-tip data is transferred there. These transfers are covered by the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses in each provider's data processing terms.
leaves.choices: When you export your data or open a link to our website, you choose where it goes.

noAds.body: Piggybow shows no ads. It doesn't track you, and it contains no advertising or analytics tools. We don't sell or share your data.

children.body: Piggybow is meant for adults. It isn't designed for children.

choices.export: Me → Export my data saves your journal as a spreadsheet file (CSV) that you can keep anywhere.
choices.delete: Me → Delete all my data erases everything Piggybow stored on your phone. On Android, copies in your phone's own backup are managed in your Google account settings.
choices.off: stay off until you turn them on, and you can turn them off anytime in Me.
choices.tips: stay off until you say yes, and you can turn them off anytime in Me → Pig tips. Without them, your pig shares its built-in tips.

changes.body: If we change this policy, we'll publish the new version on this page with a new effective date.
